subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should the remaining fix guarantee cron failure reporting from outside the wedged Gateway process, or is restart-time interrupted-run accounting plus diagnostics enough after memory fixes are proven by a macOS soak?
rationale: Source inspection shows useful in-process recovery and alert paths, but the issue's core complaint is alert silence while the same process is starved; choosing an external watchdog or supervisor-backed reporting path is a product and ownership decision.

options.title: Require soak plus externalized failure signal
options.body: Keep this issue open for macOS launchd soak proof and design a started/success/error signal that can surface stuck cron runs even when the Gateway event loop is unhealthy.

options.title: Accept restart-time accounting only
options.body: Treat startup interrupted-run marking and diagnostics as sufficient once a maintainer-provided macOS soak proves memory pressure no longer reproduces.

options.title: Split remaining work
options.body: Close the memory portion only after proof and move external failure reporting to a narrower cron reliability issue.

recommendation.title: Require soak plus externalized failure signal
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for macOS launchd soak proof and design a started/success/error signal that can surface stuck cron runs even when the Gateway event loop is unhealthy.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current-main integration and macOS Gateway routing signal among the likely owners, while memory and cron specialists can support the implementation details.
